statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress 52 (elevated) after Washington rejected Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz roadmap and with the ten-year Treasury yield at a post-crisis high of 5.18%.
recommendation: Tail stays in the 6-9 band and far below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published: a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires, and the CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls six hours beyond the end of this forecast. Elevated Stress describes a difficult environment that may still mean-revert, and is reported separately from the Tail-derived state.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6 while a rejected Hormuz roadmap and a 5.18% ten-year lift Stress to 52
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, six hours after this forecast window closes, so every assessed hour is structurally incapable of containing an observed price path. Friday's completed session argues against pathological structure rather than for it: NDX closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below its 52-week high of 30,770.63, while NQ settled at 30,889.25 roughly 108 points under its 30,997.25 high and 210 above its low. That is a two-way auction closing away from both extremes, with VIX down 5.11% to 14.87. Tail is therefore held at 6. Stress is a different question and moves up to 52. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed after President Trump rejected Tehran's seven-day reopening roadmap on Saturday and President Pezeshkian said Iran has no trust in negotiations, which withdraws the specific catalyst behind the roughly 8% weekly fall in U.S. crude to 92.41 and leaves Brent near 104.32. Long-end yields compound that: the ten-year reached 5.18% on Friday, a post-crisis high, with the official H.15 series showing 4.87% at two years and 5.47% at thirty years through 24 September. Michigan final sentiment for September printed 48.1 with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6%. Shared latest-session context was mildly constructive beneath the surface, with megacaps 6 of 8 higher and semiconductors 6 of 7 higher, but it is delayed and non-real-time and cannot establish current structure. Confidence of 80 reflects verified index, futures, volatility, yield and energy levels together with a verified seven-day calendar, discounted for the structurally absent live tape and for two unavailable sections in the shared context feed.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so none is unavailable. The window opens in the back half of Friday's U.S. cash session, where Tail ran 18-19 with EA_ON mapped throughout and Stress held in the mid-50s under a mixed mode. After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 7 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out and the mode moved to normal. Through Saturday the halt kept Tail flat at 7-8 while Stress rebuilt from 44 to 50 as the Hormuz diplomacy deteriorated, and Confidence drifted from the high 80s to 81-83 as the last tradable tape aged. No hour in the window was mapped above green, and no historical opinion has been restated with later information.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00Z on Sunday, six hours past the 16:00Z end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 6-9 band throughout and stays far below the 25 blocking threshold, mapping EA_ON and green in every slot. The step from 6 to 7 at the start of Sunday and to 8 and then 9 through Sunday is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of the single reopening auction, not observed one-way structure. Stress traces the weekend news-flow windows, easing to 49 in the thin overnight hours and building to 54 late on Sunday on the unresolved strait closure, Brent near 104 and a thirty-year yield at 5.47%. Confidence decays from 80 to 73 purely because the newest observable tape ages past 38 hours with no replacement possible before the reopen. The conditional branch that would matter is the shape of that reopen: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would validate the low Tail carried here, while immediate one-way extension holding near an extreme would be the first real amplifier.
